page.title: Company sign-in
page.description: Let people sign in with their work account instead of a FixFlow password.
page.note: Accounts made in FixFlow keep their password, so the administrator account you made here is your way back in if the directory is ever down. People who sign in through the directory get an account on their first sign-in, and the directory keeps their password.
page.load_failed: The company sign-in settings could not be loaded.

oidc.title: OpenID Connect
oidc.help: Works with Keycloak, Microsoft Entra, Okta, Google and any provider that speaks OpenID Connect. People are sent to the provider to sign in.
oidc.enabled: Offer "Sign in with" a company account
oidc.label: Name of the account on the sign-in button
oidc.label_help: The button reads "Sign in with" and this name, for example "Microsoft" or "Acme account".
oidc.issuer_help: The address of the provider's realm or tenant, for example https://keycloak.example.com/realms/acme. It must start with https.
oidc.secret_saved: Saved. Leave blank to keep it.
oidc.secret_help: Kept encrypted and never shown again. Leave it blank for a provider app that has no secret.
oidc.groups_claim: Name of the groups in the sign-in
oidc.groups_claim_help: Usually groups. For Microsoft Entra app roles, use roles.
oidc.trust_email: Trust email addresses the provider has not verified
oidc.trust_email_help: Careful: when this is on, someone who can set any email address at the provider could sign in as an existing FixFlow person. Leave it off unless only your own company's people can sign in there (a single Microsoft Entra tenant, for example).
oidc.redirect: Redirect address to register at the provider
oidc.redirect_help: Add this exact address as an allowed redirect (callback) address in the provider's app settings.
oidc.check_ok: The provider answered. Issuer: {{issuer}}. {{keys}} signing keys found.
oidc.check_failed: The provider could not be checked.

ldap.title: LDAP and Active Directory
ldap.help: People type their directory username or email and password on the FixFlow sign-in screen, and FixFlow checks them with your directory server. For Active Directory, use sAMAccountName as a login attribute, objectGUID as the ID attribute and memberOf for groups.
ldap.enabled: Sign people in through the directory server
ldap.encryption_none: None (plain, only on a trusted network)
ldap.encryption_none_warning: Without encryption, passwords cross the network in the clear. Use this only on a network you trust.
ldap.verify_help: Turn this off only for a test server. Your own certificate authority can be added below.
ldap.ca_help: Paste your company's certificate authority (PEM text) if the server uses a certificate it issued.
ldap.bind_dn_help: The distinguished name of a read-only account FixFlow uses to look people up. Leave blank if the directory allows anonymous searches.
ldap.login_attributes_help: Attributes a typed login may match, separated by commas, for example mail, uid, sAMAccountName.
ldap.id_attribute_help: A value that never changes for a person: entryUUID for OpenLDAP, objectGUID for Active Directory. Blank uses their distinguished name.
ldap.groups_attribute_help: Usually memberOf. Leave blank if the directory does not list a person's groups on the person.
ldap.group_base_help: For a directory with no memberOf: groups under here that list the person as a member are used.
ldap.check_more: There may be more: only the first few are counted.
ldap.check_failed: The directory could not be checked.

try.title: Try a person
try.help: Type a login and password to see what the directory says about them and which role they would get. Nothing is saved or signed in, and the password is not kept.
try.turned_away: Would be turned away: none of their groups gives a role.
try.not_found: Not found, or the password is wrong.
try.failed: The person could not be tried.

roles.title: Who gets which role
roles.help: Name the directory groups for each role, one per line. A group's name or its whole distinguished name both work. A person in the groups of several roles gets the highest.
roles.default: Role for people in none of these groups
roles.default_help: Choose a role to let everyone in the directory sign in, or leave it on the first choice to let only the groups above in.
roles.create_people: Make an account for people who sign in for the first time
roles.create_people_help: When this is off, only people who already have an account here can sign in through the directory.
roles.sync_roles: The role follows the groups at every sign-in
roles.sync_roles_help: When this is on, administrators cannot change the role of a directory person by hand. Even then, the last administrator is never taken from the company.
roles.nobody_warning: Name the groups for at least one role, or choose a role for everyone, before turning company sign-in on.

actions.remove_confirm: Remove the company sign-in settings? People will sign in with FixFlow passwords only, and the directory secrets are forgotten. People who signed in through the directory keep their accounts, and an administrator can give them a password.

toast.save_failed: Could not save the company sign-in settings.
